name: Han nationalism
summary: Han nationalism is an ethnic nationalism that treats ethnic Han Chinese as the core, or only true members, of the Chinese nation. It arose in the late Qing as an anti-Manchu revolutionary creed that framed Han and Manchu as rival races and sought a republic, and it survives as a cultural and online movement such as the Hanfu revival and as Han-centrism inside state nationalism. It often conflicts with the official multi-ethnic idea of the Chinese nation.
scope: The late Qing revolutionary core, based on Zou Rong's The Revolutionary Army (1903) and Zhang Binglin's racial writings, plus the modern cultural and online strand (Hanfu movement, Han-centrism, resentment of minority preferences). Han Taiwanese nationalism and the CCP's critique of 'Han chauvinism' are noted but not the basis. Economic and social-policy questions were mostly never addressed, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Zhang Binglin
keyFigures.role: Revolutionary thinker who stressed Han bloodline and made 'Han' a racial category opposed to the Manchus.

keyFigures.name: Zou Rong
keyFigures.role: Author of The Revolutionary Army (1903), the best-known anti-Manchu Han nationalist tract.

keyFigures.name: Sun Yat-sen
keyFigures.role: Led Han nationalist revolt against the Manchu Qing.

sources.usedFor: Modern cultural strand: heritage revival, Confucian values, resentment of minority preferences.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sources describe Han nationalism through race and nation, not wage policy, and adherents range from state-socialist to market views.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine takes no economic line; Zou Rong's republican program lists no market policy and modern adherents split between state-led and market positions.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the ethnic-nationalist core addresses ownership of utilities, and adherents are divided.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Zou Rong's program says everyone bears the burden of taxation but sets no progressive rate; later adherents have no common line.

unions-good.rationale: Labor organization is outside what the sources define as Han nationalism; adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Zou Rong lists natural rights including life and freedoms but the sources give no firm stance on how inviolable property is.

strong-leader.rationale: Han-centric nationalism has been fused with state nationalism under strong leaders such as Xi Jinping, but the early revolutionaries sought elected republics; mild and contested.

state-harmful.rationale: The tradition is state-building: Zou Rong demands a new central government and republic, so the state is essential, not harmful.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: The program stresses national independence and citizen soldiers, and Han nationalism links to resistance against foreign powers; a modest lean to agree.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: Zou Rong calls for a central government as general body for the whole Han nation, and the movement is unitary nationalist, so decentralization is disfavored.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented stance on penal philosophy; adherents are divided.

traditional-family.rationale: The Hanfu strand ties revival to Confucian ritual and moral self-cultivation, supporting traditional family values as part of Han cultural heritage.

abortion-legal.rationale: No documented position; adherents split between pronatalist and pragmatic views.

more-religion-public.rationale: Han nationalists favor Confucian and folk heritage but are not defined by religious public life; revival is cultural, and some online strands are hostile to Islam and Tibetan Buddhism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents resent affirmative action and legal leniency for ethnic minorities, so they reject state remedial programs framed around ethnicity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Reviving Han clothing, rites and heritage is the centre of the Hanfu movement and Han cultural nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: The founding texts call for sweeping away millennia of despotism by revolution, not gradual reform; Zhang Binglin opposed Liang Qichao's reformism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Zou Rong demands independence and no foreign interference with Chinese affairs, so ceding power to international bodies runs against the tradition.

free-trade.rationale: The founding texts resent harassment by the foreign Powers but no trade doctrine is stated; adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: The Revolutionary Army puts Han racial survival and national independence above all else, against the Powers and Manchu rule.

open-borders.rationale: A nation defined by Han ethnicity and bloodline rejects open borders as incompatible with preserving it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Zou Rong credits scientific advance with destroying superstition and despotism, so a mild pro-progress lean.

revolution-justified.rationale: The founding text is a call to revolution, and Zou Rong says people may overthrow a government that infringes their rights.

experts-over-public.rationale: No clear stance; revolutionaries favored elected assemblies while later Han-centrism fused with state authority.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A nation-centred, ethnically defined movement has no program of abolishing money or wage labor.

one-party-rule.rationale: Early revolutionaries wanted an elected republic, while the modern Han-centric strand is fused with CCP-state nationalism; adherents split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Zou Rong calls for killing the Manchu emperor as a warning that despotism must not revive and for a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: The founding text envisions elected assemblies and a president, yet modern online Han nationalists are divided and often ethnically conditional about democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Zou Rong proposes elected deputies and public elections, not direct legislation by citizens.

workers-councils.rationale: The program is a republic with elected deputies on national lines, not class-based councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Han nationalists see Tibet, Xinjiang, Mongolia and Taiwan as part of the nation or its sphere and oppose separation.

political-violence-never.rationale: Zou Rong calls for expelling or killing the Manchus and the emperor, treating violence as legitimate.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Zou Rong grounds law in natural rights and public agreement, and the strand is not scripture-based.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The program demands a central state with citizen soldiers, leaving no room for privatized defense.

military-superiority.rationale: Han nationalism pursues national strength and rejects the humiliation by foreign powers; PRC Han-centrism supports military power.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The defining claim is that ethnic Han are the true members of the Chinese nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement sees history in terms of race and nation, not class; Zhang Binglin framed conflict as Han versus Manchu.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No egalitarian economic program; ethnic hierarchy within the nation sits uneasily with this.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Han nationalists reject autonomy claims by Tibetans, Uyghurs and Mongols over their traditional lands.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Zou Rong stresses both natural rights and citizen duties of soldiering and taxation; the Confucian strand leans to duty but the question is mixed.

limit-population.rationale: No stance; Han nationalism worries about Han racial survival, which cuts against limits, while PRC policy imposed them.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The tradition embraces science and modern progress to renew the nation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pro-science but institutional continuity matters to the cultural strand; no clear position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Hanfu and cultural revival look back to pre-Qing Han order as a lost ideal, while the revolution also looks to progress; leans agree.

direct-action.rationale: The founding text urges revolution rather than elections, but modern strands operate online and within the state.

means-match-ends.rationale: Zou Rong justifies violent means to build a republic, rejecting this principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A civilizational-pride movement has no sympathy for returning to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a feature of the doctrine and incompatible with a developmental nation-state.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts a nationalism founded on ethnic nation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement attributes conflict to race and foreign aggression rather than capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Zou Rong's program says everyone has a duty to bear the burden of taxation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are tied to membership in the Han nation, a group, in this doctrine, though Zou Rong also lists natural individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Zou Rong's program states that all men have a duty to serve as citizen soldiers.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement is about belonging to a nation and its state, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: A nationalism of blood and heritage rejects citizens as customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Some online adherents claim hostile elites; the sources give no firm line.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial nationalism treats Han bloodline as the basis of identity, with Zhang Binglin stressing it as proof of China's greatness.

total-state.rationale: Early revolutionaries wanted limited republican government; not a total-state doctrine.

national-rebirth.rationale: Hanfu proponents tie revival to national rejuvenation, and Zou Rong calls for a complete cleansing and renewal of the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The article links Han superiority ideas to historic expansion, and some extremists say Tibetans, Mongols and Uyghurs belong to a wider Han family; contested.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The program rests on elected assemblies and public agreement, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Zou Rong declares equality, no distinction of base and noble, and natural freedoms.

revive-national-language.rationale: The Hanfu strand revives Han traditional culture; Mandarin is already the state language, so this is a weak inference.

rule-by-example.rationale: Confucian-influenced revival values moral self-cultivation, but the early revolutionary text relies on law and elected government.

national-self-determination.rationale: Zou Rong demands independence for the Han nation and says Han should preserve their independence as a people among world powers.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Zou Rong credits science over superstition but modern adherents are not defined by this.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage revival is the center of the Hanfu movement; sacrificing it is opposite.

dominated-front.rationale: Zou Rong sees China harassed by the Powers, and Han nationalism includes resistance to Western imperialism; no documented call for a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Nation-first ethnic nationalism holds that people organize as a nation rather than as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Zou Rong declares men and women equal, but the traditionalist Hanfu strand leans conservative; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Han racism targets Manchus and minorities but the sources do not describe segregation laws; Zhang Binglin sought expulsion, so mild disagree only.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The nationalist view of the state is as an ethnic instrument, not a class tool, so mild disagreement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Han-centrism expects minorities and newcomers to adopt Han culture; the article describes Han civilising narratives and sinicization of Xinjiang.

elite-replacement.rationale: The sources do not document a replacement conspiracy theory for Han nationalism; some strands do blame elites for minority preferences.

proportional-representation.rationale: Zou Rong proposes elected deputies from each province without specifying electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Han nationalism emphasizes the Han nation, not spreading a regime abroad, though civilising narratives exist.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Zou Rong declares equality but the movement does not use structural-patriarchy analysis; weak disagree.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Zou Rong denounces the Manchu court and Qing elite as corrupt and tyrannical; the modern strand frames elites as corrupt toward minorities.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants a strong state defending nation and heritage, beyond night-watchman role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement values Han bloodline purity and Han nationalists oppose assimilation of others into the nation; Zhang Binglin stressed bloodline.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Han racial hierarchy over Manchus and minorities conflicts with equal rights before the law, though Zou Rong asserts equality among Han citizens.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not part of the ideology; nationalism favors national road.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Han settlement into Tibet, Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia is framed by adherents as legitimate national migration, so they reject this label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Han-centric view opposes special legal treatment for minorities and wants one law for all.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of Han practice; beef consumption is common and the cause is Hindu.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Zou Rong says governments rest on public agreement and may be overthrown when they infringe rights, though the consent is that of Han people.

population-transfer.rationale: Zou Rong and Zhang Binglin called for expelling the Manchus; Zhang preferred expulsion to Manchuria.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The founding text calls for expelling or killing Manchus and the emperor, which is initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The text draws on Social Darwinist racial theories where peoples compete for survival, per the scholarly account.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Zou Rong speaks of being slaves under Manchus, resembling non-domination, but no theoretical stance is stated.

separated-powers.rationale: Zou Rong proposes a central government with elected deputies and no detail on checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: A class vanguard is not a feature of ethnic nationalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The core claim is that only Han belong to the nation and diversity threatens its cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Zou Rong proposes election, not lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The strong-state, security view supports emergency powers against separatists, but it is not directly documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: Early adherents demanded freedom of the press, while the PRC-fused strand accepts party control; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Split between ROC-era and PRC-fused strands.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A Han-ethnic definition of the nation favors strict conditions on citizenship.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Zou Rong rejects foreign rights over China, and nationalism rejects pooled sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Zou Rong envisages a president, but no detail on command.

clerical-rule.rationale: The program is a secular republic with science against superstition.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalism supports national survival in war; defeatism contradicts it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Confucian moral outlook leans toward censorship while revolutionaries valued free speech; split.

recall-officials.rationale: Zou Rong says people may overthrow a government that infringes their rights, a weak parallel to recall.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Han nationalism, including Han Taiwanese strands, supports Han unity under one state or sees Taiwan as part of the Han nation; Taiwanese strand diverges, so medium.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Han superiority and civilizing narratives are documented in the Han-centric tradition.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Zou Rong championed science against superstition.

minority-language-support.rationale: Han-centric adherents resent minority preferences and favor Han culture's primacy.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The strand resents leniency for minorities, so it opposes special exemptions.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Zou Rong's program has deputies elected and rights publicly discussed to set up a new government.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The PRC-fused strand accepts this, while early revolutionaries championed freedoms; contested.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: National strength is a core goal and the movement opposes dependence on foreign powers.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Zou Rong's program has the provisional president elected by the deputies, not directly; weak agree.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Han nationalists claim Tibet, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia and Taiwan, refusing concessions.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents defend Chinese control of Tibet and Xinjiang as legitimate, so reject this label.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Han nationalists oppose secession by Tibet, Xinjiang and Taiwan and back force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Han nationalists resist special autonomy arrangements and favor Han-dominant unity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Zou Rong attacks the doctrine that heaven makes emperors and calls for killing the emperor.

character-from-environment.rationale: Racial nationalism stresses bloodline, over upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Zou Rong declares despotism overthrown by rights and a government that employs power to defend popular rights.

leader-cult.rationale: PRC-fused strand tolerates it, early revolutionaries did not; split.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Some Han nationalists claim wider Han-family territory and kin peoples; contested but central to expansionist strands.

women-must-cover.rationale: Zou Rong declares women equal citizens, and Han nationalists oppose Islamic dress as alien.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Some extremists claim wider Han family, while the core is Han-only; split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Han-centric adherents oppose autonomy and preferences for minorities within the state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement explains history through race and nation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolutionary Han nationalists such as Zou Rong and Sun Yat-sen organized armed uprisings against the Qing.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Zou Rong abolishes distinctions of noble and base and overthrows the imperial system.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural revival is Han-centered, and Han history is taught as central.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The article notes narratives of Tibetan backwardness and Han civilizing; held by Han-centric adherents.

patriotic-education.rationale: Han-centrism fused with state nationalism backs patriotic education.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The article notes Han superiority links to historic expansion into Korea, Vietnam and Central Asia.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Zou Rong lists inalienable rights, but no constitutional entrenchment is stated.

elective-rulers.rationale: Zou Rong provides for the provisional president to be elected by deputies chosen by public vote.

minority-veto.rationale: The program envisions majority decisions by elected bodies.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Zou Rong says that when a government infringes rights, people may overthrow it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Zou Rong's program has a general assembly of elected deputies; weak.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The founding text calls the nation to revolution.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Zou Rong notes harassment by the Powers, but no dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Ethnic definitions of nation favor reserving office for the national core.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Han nationalists link to historic claims and resentment of the Century of Humiliation.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Han nationalism holds Han primacy and rejects indigenous leadership claims.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Hanfu and Han-cultural strand insists on authentic Han forms, extending to national institutions.

filial-duty.rationale: Confucian values that the cultural revival ties to Han heritage emphasize filial piety.

single-official-language.rationale: Han-centrism pushes Mandarin as the sole common language; sinicization is noted.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The strand resents racial preferences for minorities.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Hanfu strand includes conspiracy theories about a Manchu plot, according to Carrico.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Zou Rong rejects foreign intervention and demands sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is ethnic, not religious.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Han-centric views of the Chinese dynasties include tribute but modern adherents are split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Split between ROC and PRC strands.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Sources address race and nation, not capitalism, and adherents range from state-socialist to market views.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The sources do not place Han nationalism on this axis; adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Adherents range from state-socialist to market views, and the ideology does not claim to combine left and right.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Zou Rong grounded the revolution in natural rights and popular sovereignty, not divine authority.

property-franchise.rationale: Zou Rong's republic rests on natural rights and equal citizens; no wealth qualification is documented.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Never addressed; the doctrine is about race and nation, and an ecofeminist reading is not part of it.

racial-franchise.rationale: The anti-Manchu program aimed to place government in Han hands and to expel or exclude Manchus, so political rights were framed for the Han.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Economic questions were never central to the doctrine, and adherents range from anti-capitalist revolutionaries to market-friendly online nationalists.

rent-control.rationale: Sources describe Han nationalism through race and nation, not housing policy, and adherents range widely on economics.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Zou Rong calls the Han descendants of the Yellow Emperor and Han nationalism stresses a Han bloodline reaching back to antiquity.

culture-before-state.rationale: The late Qing strand put revolution and a Han state first, while the modern Hanfu strand puts cultural revival first, so adherents split.

person-over-state.rationale: Zou Rong invokes natural rights and citizenship, but the nation-first framing pulls the other way, so adherents are split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Han nationalism treats Han as a race whose interests oppose those of other groups, as in Zou Rong's anti-Manchu tract and Zhang Binglin's racial writings.

racial-pride.rationale: The movement is built on pride in Han descent and ancestry, from the Yellow Emperor myth of the late Qing to the Hanfu revival.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anti-Manchu revolution was offensive in aim, while modern adherents split on irredentist claims; no settled position.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Han nationalism is strongly suspicious of foreign influence and minority separatism (Tibet, Xinjiang, Taiwan) as threats to China's integrity, though a specific plot is not a doctrinal tenet.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Han as a descended, enduring race-nation (Yellow Emperor lineage) is the movement's core, so it treats the nation as a lasting community of meaning.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The doctrine never weighed the environment against liberty, and adherents plausibly split, so it is left neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Han nationalists have said nothing on union membership rules, so the movement is indifferent.

race-social-construct.rationale: Zhang Binglin and Zou Rong treated Han as a distinct race of common descent, so race as a mere construct is rejected.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement has no stated view on state gender-equality bodies, and adherents are split between traditionalists and others.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement resents minority preferences and treats the nation as Han-centred, so ethnic territorial autonomy is opposed.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Zou Rong and later Han nationalists present Han as descendants of the Yellow Emperor with a homeland to recover from alien rule.

self-ownership.rationale: Zou Rong's text sets out natural rights of citizens as part of the revolutionary programme.

missingStatements.text: The ruling dynasty or elite of a different ethnic origin than the majority has no legitimate claim to rule the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: The anti-Manchu revolution rested on branding the Qing as an alien race, and Zou Rong called for overthrowing the Manchu government.

missingStatements.text: The people should adopt the traditional dress and rites of their ancestors in preference to those imposed or influenced by foreign rulers.
missingStatements.rationale: The Hanfu movement revives pre-Qing dress over qipao and tangzhuang, which it links to Manchu rule.

missingStatements.text: The nation descends from a common ancestor, and that bloodline is the basis of its identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Zou Rong calls Han the descendants of the Yellow Emperor and Zhang Binglin stressed Han bloodline.

notes: Han nationalism is distinct from official Chinese nationalism, whose multi-ethnic framing the CCP defends, and the PRC treats 'Han chauvinism' as a fault. Han Taiwanese nationalism diverges on unification. Few of the 312 statements touch the movement's concerns, so most answers are inferred and low-confidence.
